title: Fix the verification skills to the verify-app constant and cut the compose-into-the-test-command step
action:
Two skill bodies, one serial pass, one `bee dev regen` at the end. Edit ONLY the sources under `skills/`; the rendered copies under `.claude/`, `.agents/`, `.opencode/`, `.claude-plugin/` and `.codex-plugin/` are written by regen and are never hand-edited.

PART A — the constant name and path (per D1 d0e3c3a0 and D8 9f4f90f0).

`verify-<app>` becomes the literal `verify-app`, identical in every repo, and the source path becomes `.bee/verify/verify-app/`. Find every site with `rg -n 'verify-<app>|verify-\$|\.bee/verify' skills/bee-verifying/SKILL.md skills/bee-verify-upkeep/SKILL.md` — 9 hits in bee-verifying, 4 in bee-verify-upkeep at the time of writing. The generated skill's frontmatter `name:` becomes `verify-app`; the app's identity moves into its `description`, which is what routing actually reads. Do NOT prefix it `bee-`: `packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/onboard/skills.rs:954` proves the bee-* sync emits `remove_skill` for any bee-named target directory absent from bee's own source, so a `bee-verify-app` would be deleted from every runtime skill home on the next `bee onboard --apply`.

In `bee-verify-upkeep`, step 0 'Locate the target' now has nothing to locate — the path is a constant. Find it with `rg -n 'Locate the target'` and delete the step, renumbering the rest.

PART B — remove the composition (per D6 2a8eac15).

`commands.test` stays pure tests. The drive no longer composes into it. Section headings in `bee-verifying` at the time of writing, found with `rg -n '^#+ ' skills/bee-verifying/SKILL.md`:

  - `## 5. Ask the second question, then compose the drive into the test command` — its premise is gone; retitle it for what survives.
  - `### Two moments, never one yes` — DELETE. It exists only to gate the config write.
  - `### Compose: append, never replace` — DELETE.
  - `### Always \`bash <path>\`, never a bare path` — DELETE THE SECTION, KEEP THE FACT. It records why a rendered copy is invoked as `bash <path>`: bee's render leaves source `0755` and every rendered copy `0644`, so a bare path fails with `Permission denied` on a host's first onboard. That reason must survive somewhere a reader still reaches — it is now needed wherever the drive is invoked for a cap proof. Choose the home and say so.
  - `### Where to write it` — DELETE. It is the hand-edit procedure for `commands.test`.
  - `### Fast and full: the contract the control script must satisfy` — KEEP the two drive scopes; they still matter. REWRITE its claim that 'The FAST drive is what composes into the declared test command'. Per D5 (036e8a79) the fast drive is what a worker runs for a user-facing cell's cap proof, recorded as `green:live`; the full drive is the periodic sweep. Nothing is written into `commands.test`.

Read `## 6. Offer the maintenance loop` and anything after it for surviving references to composition, the second consent moment, or a measured-cost question — remove what the deletion orphans.

PART C — the composed-host line (per plan.md Decisions taken 3).

A host that already composed a drive into its test command is LEFT ALONE. bee never edits `commands.test`. Add one line to `bee-verify-upkeep`: when the declared test command contains a drive path, REPORT it to the user with the reason, never rewrite it. State plainly that removing it is the user's call.

FINALLY: run `.bee/bin/bee dev regen` so every rendered copy matches its source, then `.bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check`. A source edit without the regen leaves five stale copies.
